title: Motoko Functions and the Candid User Interface
section: 38. Build Your First Defi (Decentralised Finance) DApp - DBANK
summary: Adds functions to the DBank actor: private then public, with a typed Nat parameter. Shows calling canister methods through dfx canister call and through the generated Candid UI, and ends with a challenge to write a withdraw function.

concepts.heading: Defining functions with func
points: Functions use the `func` keyword (Swift-like), then a name, parameter list in parentheses and a body in braces. First version: topUp with no parameters that adds 1 to currentValue.
Finish the function with a print of the new value (Debug.print with debug_show).
The closing brace of a function declaration needs a semicolon after it; leaving it out causes errors. Motoko expects a semicolon after every declaration.
Calling it inside the actor body (`topUp();`) runs it at deploy time, so the printed value is one higher (101 in the demo).

concepts.heading: Private vs public functions
points: A plain func is private: it can only be used inside the actor's braces.
Trying `dfx canister call dbank topUp` against a private function errors with a message saying the canister has no update method with that name.
Add `public` before func to expose it to the outside world (command line, other canisters, a frontend). Redeploy with dfx deploy after editing.

concepts.heading: Calling canister methods from the CLI
points: Syntax: `dfx canister call <canister-name> <function-name> [argument]`. The canister name comes from dfx.json / the project (lowercase dbank in the lecture).
Arguments go in parentheses, in Candid syntax, e.g. `(12)`; with no inputs nothing is needed.

concepts.heading: Candid UI
points: Candid is an interface description language: it describes a canister's public methods and types, independent of the language it was written in (Motoko, Rust). Candid UI reads that description and builds a clickable test page, comparable to the try-it-out section of interactive API docs.
Setup: get the Candid UI canister ID with `dfx canister id __Candid_UI` (two leading underscores). Open the local replica address with `?canisterId=<that id>` in the query string.
The page then asks for the ID of your own canister: get it with `dfx canister id dbank` and paste it in. A .did file is not needed, so ignore that prompt. Press Go.
The UI lists each public function with a Call button and input fields. Results/prints still appear in the terminal running dfx start.
After changing the code and redeploying, refresh the Candid UI page to see new or changed functions.

concepts.heading: Parameters and the Nat type
points: Add a parameter inside the parentheses as `name : Type`. Here `amount : Nat`.
Nat is a natural number: zero and above, no negatives or decimals. Candid UI shows a numeric field and states that it expects a natural number.
Replace the fixed +1 with `currentValue += amount;`. `+=` and `-=` are compound-assign operators like JavaScript.

concepts.heading: State resets on redeploy
points: After redeploying, the balance went back to its initial value (100), so a top-up of 12 gave 112 rather than 103+12. Each dfx deploy re-initialised the variables in this version.
The lecture defers the explanation to the orthogonal persistence lesson.

task.name: Write a withdraw function
task.starting_point: The DBank actor with a public topUp(amount : Nat) function and Candid UI working.
task.goal: Add a public function that subtracts a given amount from currentValue and prints the result.
steps: Declare `public func withdraw(amount : Nat)` (a public function so Candid UI and the CLI can reach it).
Print the new value with Debug.print(debug_show(currentValue)); end the function with a semicolon.
Run dfx deploy, refresh Candid UI, call the function with an amount such as 10 and check the terminal shows the lower balance.
task.expected_result: Withdrawing 10 from 100 prints 90. Withdrawing more than the balance traps with a natural-subtraction underflow error, which the next lesson fixes with conditionals.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 38 - Build Your First Defi (Decentralised Finance) DApp - DBANK/38.03 Motoko Functions and the Candid User Interface/DBANK/src/DBANK/main.mo

pitfalls: Forgetting the semicolon after a function's closing brace.
Calling a function that is not public: the CLI says there is no such update method.
Forgetting to redeploy and refresh Candid UI after edits.
Mixing up the Candid UI canister id and your own canister id.
Assuming the balance survives a redeploy (it does not yet).
Withdrawing more than the balance: Nat underflow error.
(Extra) The reference repo spells the function topUP, so CLI calls must use that exact casing.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (no section 38 file).
gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Motoko functions and Candid UI': explain func, public, parameters and Nat.

Tasks: (1) write topUp with a Nat input; (2) make it public and explain why the CLI call fails otherwise; (3) write withdraw; (4) predict the output of withdraw(500) on a balance of 100; (5) list the commands needed to open Candid UI.
Interactive demo idea: a simulated Candid UI with buttons for the user's functions, a mock terminal log and a toggle between public and private that changes whether the function appears.
